// The fixed shape of the same two tests: every path a tool WRITES is named
// inside t.TempDir(), so the run leaves nothing in the tree. The scanner reads
// this file and finds nothing, which is the other half of the contract -- a
// rule that only ever says yes is not a rule.
package fixture

import (
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

func TestFirstRunExampleRuns(t *testing.T) {
	graph := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "deps.json")
	if code, _, stderr := runCLI(t, "dependencies", "--graph", graph, "--node", "b"); code != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("the usage example does not run: exit %d, stderr: %s", code, stderr)
	}
}

func TestPacketIsWrittenWhereItIsAsked(t *testing.T) {
	var out, errb bytes.Buffer
	packet := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "packet.md")
	if code := run([]string{"packet", "--who", "emma", "--out", packet}, &out, &errb); code != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("packet exit=%d stderr=%s", code, errb.String())
	}
}
